requirements.requirement: node2 has SNMPv2c access to node1 using the designated branch-readonly community
requirements.summary: Direct SNMPv2c queries from node2 succeeded before and after both restarts, and node1's configuration matched the same runtime community variable. However, the captured commands never reveal that $SNMP_COMMUNITY expanded specifically to the literal branch-readonly, so the designated value is not directly verifiable.

requirements.requirement: Expose system identity, uptime, sysLocation West Branch, and sysContact ops@branch.test
requirements.summary: node2 directly read sysDescr, sysUpTime, sysContact, sysName, and sysLocation with the required contact and location values. The same values remained readable after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Permit community reads but reject writes
requirements.summary: Reads succeeded, repeated snmpset attempts returned noAccess, and subsequent reads confirmed sysLocation remained West Branch. Final configuration also showed a read-only community and no rwcommunity entry.
The asset-register.csv file on both nodes retained the baseline SHA-256 da19717ac6440a3f765b43e60902dc7670b3d3ef133daa4a009a5f726fc6509a, including after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. EL7 Net-SNMP 5.7.2-49 packages were installed and demonstrated working behavior after reboot.

overall_summary: The required SNMP behavior, values, write rejection, asset preservation, and legacy-platform retention are directly demonstrated. The only material evidentiary gap is that the literal community value was hidden behind $SNMP_COMMUNITY. The provider restart protocol was otherwise strong on both nodes: healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, observed unavailability, changed boot identities, and recovered service, data, and SNMP behavior were captured; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor observations.
limitations: The captured evidence does not show the value assigned to $SNMP_COMMUNITY, so it cannot independently confirm that the working community was literally branch-readonly.
Package-health collection timed out before and after execution on both nodes, so package-manager consistency—particularly after node2's direct RPM installation—was not independently established.
Requirement req-4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: Core package, configuration, firewall, service, and reboot mutations had clear roles. Unnecessary retained mutation: cmd-431575fef1904c6c installed net-snmp-utils on node1 even though only the agent was needed there. cmd-a521afd530114523 created /tmp/c7vault.repo during an unsuccessful node2 installation attempt; it remained. Task-related temporary artifacts were also not cleaned: /tmp/c7vault.repo on node1 from cmd-431575fef1904c6c, downloaded RPMs under /tmp/snmp-rpms from cmd-9aefb5ced3874a9e, and reboot logs from cmd-708c382132e24d3d and cmd-8701c7d49a744315 all remained. These were bounded and low risk; no failed services or broad persistent damage was observed. The failed cmd-6dbc1626eb4c466d retry has no evidence of package mutation, so it is not penalized.
